newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian Gold -- Support seen at $350, HK supply tight.
newsitem.headline: Asian Gold -- Support seen at $350, HK supply tight.

text.p: Bullion traders in Asia on Friday saw gold markets trading in a narrow range short term with support at the US$350 per ounce level, while Hong Kong dealers worried over the continued kilobar supply tightness.
Physical demand and mining costs would keep the price of gold around $350 per ounce or above, bullion sources said.
"We are now seeing the results from physical business and there is support just below $352 per ounce," said a Hong Kong trader at an international bank.
A Singapore trader noted that "after the aggressive selling seen early this year, we see some consolidation. The market is stabilising around $352 currently."
Gold price levels were unlikely to move below the $350 mark, another Singapore source noted.
"The cost of mining, which is the cost of production, is currently around $300-$320 per ounce, so I don't think prices would fall by between eight to 10 percent from current levels," he said.
Hong Kong gold at midday (0430 GMT) was trading at $354.00/50 per ounce, down from its opening level of $354.30/80 and slightly below New York's Thursday close at $354.10/60.
Bullion dealers in Hong Kong expressed surprise at the continued shortage in kilobar supplies.
"I thought it would be alright by now," a physical dealer in Hong Kong said.
Traders said the shortage was caused by refineries getting back to work only slowly after the Christmas and New Year break.
Some said that tighter gold lease rates made it more expensive to ship gold to Hong Kong.
Gold premiums in Hong Kong were still around 150 U.S. cents, compared to about 70 U.S. cents a few weeks ago.
The next two weeks were expected to be peak demand periods, Hong Kong and Singapore traders said.
A Singapore-based jeweller said the "bright spot" in the current soft market was the potential demand for gold from China ahead of the Chinese New Year holiday period in early February.
"That (Chinese New Year demand) may spark some recovery in prices but breaking the $360 mark would be difficult," he added.
Gold dealers in Singapore said spot prices were likely to continue it their current trend and remain rangebound between $350-$360 an ounce over the next two weeks.
"But the market undertone is still a shade soft with talk of the central banks still selling gold," said the trader."There is less momentum for it to move upward than downwards."
